reasoning.reason: Your app keeps live websocket connections open (socket.io chat) — it needs an always-on server process, not a serverless platform that kills idle connections.
You expect an early-launch audience (100-1K users, ~100 live at once) — the smallest always-on tier covers this comfortably; paying for more would be capacity you never use.
Postgres is required and this plan includes a managed Postgres add-on on the same platform, avoiding a second vendor for the database.

alternatives.why_rejected: Also fits the websocket requirement, but costs more for the same class of instance and its free Postgres tier expires after 30 days.
Raw VPS requires you to manage the OS, deploys, and Postgres yourself — unnecessary operational load for a pre-launch team.
